correctness.rationale: The infected coordinates preserve their initial zero/positive support. The compact population simplex and graph Laplacian permit an exact risk-weighted Lyapunov function with negative sum-of-squares derivative. Its zero-dissipation set equals the complete equilibrium set, yielding omega-limit confinement. The finitely many equilibrium components have distinct Lyapunov levels F(r) for r<N/k; positive growth of an initially seeded lower-risk cell excludes convergence to any larger-risk component. This proves the global seed-minimum selection. The endemic Jacobian, ordered by off-risk infection, susceptible, and tied infection, is block triangular; its susceptible block dL-diag(D) is strictly negative definite, the off-risk invasion exponents have explicit signs, and its zero block is semisimple. Conservation removes exactly one zero. The closed DFE global-stability boundary follows from the same Lyapunov function and explicit infection exponents. A standard-library exact-rational checker reconstructs representative Jacobians from the source equations and verifies conservation/dissipation and the claimed spectra.

originality.rationale: The motivating two-strain source assumes positive infected dispersal and explicitly identifies complete infected lockdown as an unstudied future problem. The closest single-strain continuum paper already establishes an analogous initial-support/risk-selection phenomenon, so no general novelty is assigned to that principle. Its single-strain PDE does not state the exact finite-patch, two-strain equilibrium components, cross-strain tie constraints, and complete local invasion eigenvalue multiset. Separate one-strain positive-dispersal patch work studies a different regime and also does not dominate the claim. Targeted literature and published-record searches found no same-object result.
residual_risks: Analogous one-strain minimizer selection is established in degenerate continuum epidemic literature. The two-strain proof adapts its dissipation idea and uniqueness is source-specific, not a claim to invent the method.
An equivalent general multistrain finite-graph zero-mobility theorem might exist under different terminology that source-title and model-alias searches did not retrieve.

The later single-strain equilibrium-curve article has restricted full-text access; its accessible model and abstract concern a one-strain positive-infected-mobility patch system and do not present the accepted two-strain theorem. Its uninspected details remain a limited comparison risk.
For several tied seeded risk minima the theorem proves convergence to a simplex face, not convergence of each infection share to a distinct point.

value.rationale: The motivating two-strain paper explicitly leaves a full infected-population lockdown unstudied. The result supplies a complete natural classification, for every positive connected symmetric patch network and any susceptible mobility, of disease-free and endemic risk-indexed equilibrium strata, open versus tied coexistence, which initially seeded risk can persist, and the exact number of unstable directions at every equilibrium. The seed-contingent nature of exclusion distinguishes true lockdown from merely small infected travel and has direct conceptual value for invasion and intervention modeling; the exact Morse indices and neutral tie-simplexes are structural and not just a single simulation or renamed parameter.
